facts.raw_span: asymptomatic red to brown macules and papules
symmetrically distributed and did not coalesce
Face, distal extremities, and mucous membranes were unaffected
some lesions had resolved spontaneously with residual hyperpigmentation
hypereosinophilia (4220/μL; reference range 50-250/μL)
elevated tryptase (33.7 ng/mL; reference range <11.5 ng/mL)
elevated vitamin B12 (>6000 pg/mL; reference range 211-911 pg/mL)
Negative serologic tests for HIV, hepatitis A, B, and C
no pathologic findings on CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis
Nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils in upper dermis
FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene positive on RT-PCR
Hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia and increased eosinophils (20%, reference range <5%)

concepts.why: The patient's hypereosinophilia, FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene positivity, and hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia and increased eosinophils are consistent with Chronic Eosinophilic Leukemia.

The nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils in the skin biopsy is suggestive of Histiocytosis, although the lack of CD1a positivity and presence of stabilin 1 positivity may indicate a non-Langerhans cell type.
The elevated tryptase and vitamin B12 levels are consistent with Mastocytosis, and the skin lesions could be consistent with Cutaneous Mastocytosis.
The patient's asymptomatic red to brown macules and papules, symmetrically distributed and without coalescence, could be consistent with Eosinophilic Dermatitis.
The patient's hypereosinophilia and hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia could be consistent with a Myeloproliferative Neoplasm, although the specific diagnosis would require further evaluation.
